text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Discussions open between government and Mobil on building an electric power plant supplied with gas associated with crude oil production.

- A group set up by government to explore the possibility of exporting solid minerals says $390 million would be needed to develop the sector. Included are; iron, coal, salt, tar, kaolin, gold and talc.
- Flour millers accuse bakers of breaching an agreement intended to bring down the price of bread. Although millers reduced the price of flour, the price of bread has risen.

- Government may next year drop used vehicles from the list of goods that need to be covered by an import duty report, to increase the number being brought into Nigeria instead of neighbouring countries.
- National Fertiliser Co has shut down its second largest plant, near Onne in southeastern Nigeria for undisclosed reason.

- About 20 billion naira is to be spent by the government's Petroleum Trust Fund on schools and health institutions. Consultants have been sent across the country to identify the institutions most badly in need of rehabilitation.
- Nigerian Telecommunications will on Monday begin laying a submarine fibre optic cable linking Lagos telephones with oil producing areas in southeastern Nigeria.
